claims.text: Applying a thin reactive Ni or Ni-based HEA interlayer to W surfaces before consolidation creates a graded W–Cu interface.
The graded interlayer suppresses phase separation at the W–Cu interface.
The graded interlayer suppresses interfacial void formation.
The interlayer treatment enhances thermal conductivity and interfacial integrity under high heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
Untreated W-particle/Cu-matrix or W-ligament/Cu-matrix composites are prone to phase separation and interfacial void development during processing and service.
Magnetron sputtering before consolidation can deposit the proposed reactive interlayer on W surfaces.
Appropriate interlayer thickness and composition can promote controlled interdiffusion while avoiding brittle intermetallic phases.
Spark plasma sintering at 1000–1200 °C is an applicable consolidation window for the interlayer-treated W–Cu composite.
The treated composite is applicable under service temperatures up to approximately 1500 °C and irradiation fluxes relevant to plasma-facing-component joints.
The interlayer forms a continuous compositional transition from W through Ni or Ni-based HEA to Cu.
The continuous compositional transition smooths chemical gradients and reduces abrupt interfaces that can nucleate voids.
The reactive interlayer facilitates controlled interdiffusion at the W–Cu interface during spark plasma sintering.
Controlled interdiffusion produces a diffusion-mediated transition zone.
The diffusion-mediated graded interface reduces interfacial stresses during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Reduced interfacial stress lowers void nucleation during thermal cycling and irradiation.
Reduced void nucleation and the graded transition zone improve interfacial bonding and thermal conductivity.

Relative to untreated controls, treated composites will have significantly higher thermal conductivity, fewer interfacial voids, and greater stability after high-thermal-flux and irradiation exposure.
Formation of brittle phases can negate the effectiveness of the interlayer treatment.
